name: OpenBao CLI
description: Installs the OpenBao CLI (https://openbao.org), the open-source Vault fork, as a release binary at /usr/local/bin/bao, verified against the release's checksums.txt. Owns the login state as a named volume at OPENBAO_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/devcontainer-features/openbao (bao's token helper, set through BAO_CONFIG_PATH, keeps the token in it) so `bao login` survives rebuilds, with the post-create hook openbao-setup, and installs dcf-secret, the one command the collection's Features use to read and write secrets (get, put, status, with fixed exit codes). Mode client (the default) is the CLI against a server of yours (set BAO_ADDR in containerEnv). Mode server also runs a server inside the container, started at post-start with raft storage on the same volume and sealed until the Operator unseals it: tasks openbao:init (unseal shares printed only to a terminal, a backup choice asked for), openbao:unseal, openbao:seal, userpass login for the Operator, loopback-bound AppRole roles (openbao:approle:issue) and openbao:server:status. Onboarding: openbao:onboard:export and :onboard:claim (a starter instance restored, then rotate-keys and every access the sender held revoked) and openbao:wrap and :unwrap (one-use response-wrapping tokens for a few keys against a central server).

installTaskfile.description: Also install this Feature's Taskfile into /usr/local/share/go-task/includes.d so its tasks appear under the <id>: namespace of a root Taskfile that includes /usr/local/share/go-task/features.yml (see the go-task Feature).

mode.description: How the Feature is used. 'client' (default): the bao CLI and dcf-secret against a server outside the container (BAO_ADDR). 'server': also run a server in the container (raft storage on the Feature's volume, loopback only, started at post-start, sealed until `task openbao:unseal`; needs OpenBao 2.4.0 or newer). Override per container with OPENBAO_SETUP_MODE in containerEnv.

version.description: OpenBao release to install (e.g. '2.7.1', with or without a leading 'v'), or 'latest'. Match your OpenBao server's version.
